_status: DRAFT CROSSWALK — scholarly-knowledge based, NOT verified against ingested texts of Plutarch or Dio; every mapping must be re-verified when those texts are acquired. This file is a retrieval aid, never evidence.

_conventions.periocha_anchor: verbatim 3-8 word Latin phrase from the book's periocha (machine-validated as substring); null for books 136-137 whose periochae are lost
_conventions.plutarch: Life name with chapter range where reasonably confident; Life name alone where not; empty array where no Life covers the ground
_conventions.dio: 'frr. book N (Zonaras x.y)' for the fragmentary pre-69 BCE range (Zonaras cited only where his epitome of Dio survives, i.e. down to 146 BCE; for 146-69 BCE only Excerpta fragments exist, conventionally grouped as books 22-35); plain book.chapter numbers for extant Dio 36-56
_conventions.confidence: high only for unmistakable mappings; medium for standard but chapter-level-uncertain mappings; low for era-level or thin coverage

11.note: Curius Dentatus, Aesculapius, lex Hortensia; no Plutarch Life covers this ground.

12.periocha_anchor: Pyrrhus, Epirotarum rex, ut auxilium Tarentinis ferret
12.note: Senones, Tarentine incident, Pyrrhus crosses to Italy.

13.note: Heraclea, Fabricius and Cineas embassies, Appius Claudius speech, Asculum.

14.note: Sicily, Beneventum, expulsion from Italy; periocha also records Pyrrhus' death (Plutarch Pyrrhus 31-34, at Argos).

15.periocha_anchor: Victis Tarentinis pax et libertas data est
15.note: Fall of Tarentum, punishment of the Campanian legion at Regium.

16.periocha_anchor: Origo Carthaginiensium et primordia urbis eorum
16.note: Outbreak of First Punic War, Mamertines, Hiero; no relevant Plutarch Life.

17.periocha_anchor: C. Duillius consul aduersus classem Poenorum prospere pugnauit
17.note: Mylae, Sardinia-Corsica operations, Regulus crosses to Africa.

18.periocha_anchor: Atilius Regulus in Africa serpentem portentosae magnitudinis
18.note: Regulus in Africa, Xanthippus, captivity and embassy; no Plutarch Life of Regulus.

19.periocha_anchor: uicta ad Aegates insulas classe Poenorum

20.note: Interwar years: Gallic invasion, Insubres, Marcellus' spolia opima over Vertomarus/Viridomarus, Illyrian wars.

46.periocha_anchor: L. Aemilius Paulus, qui Persen vicerat, mortuus
46.note: Post-Pydna diplomacy (Eumenes, Prusias, Ariarathes); death of Aemilius Paulus. Zonaras thins out here; Dio book number conventional.

47.periocha_anchor: inter Masinissam et Carthaginienses de agro iudicarent
47.note: Diplomatic decade 160-154; Dalmatian war; no Plutarch Life covers it directly.

48.note: Cato vs Scipio Nasica on war with Carthage; Scipio Aemilianus in Spain.

49.note: War declared, siege of Carthage begun; Cato's 'umbras volitare' praise of Scipio is at Cato Major 27; Galba trial; Andriscus.

50.periocha_anchor: Masinissa Numidiae rex maior nonaginta annis decessit
50.note: Death of Masinissa, Scipio's irregular consulship, Pseudophilippus defeated; Plutarch's Scipio Aemilianus is lost.

51.periocha_anchor: magno labore obsessa et per partes capta est
51.note: Fall and destruction of Carthage, 146 BCE; Plutarch's Scipio Aemilianus is lost.

52.note: Achaean war, destruction of Corinth; rise of Viriathus.

53.periocha_anchor: Appius Claudius consul Salassos, gentem Alpinam, domuit
53.note: Thin periocha; second Pseudophilippus, Celtiberian operations.

54.periocha_anchor: Viriathus a proditoribus consilio Servilii Caepionis interfectus est
54.note: Numantine treaty voided, murder of Viriathus; no Plutarch Life.

55.note: Mancinus disaster at Numantia; Ti. Gracchus as quaestor negotiated the treaty (Plutarch Ti. Gracchus 5-7).

56.note: Mancinus handed over and refused; first Sicilian slave war begins (Eunus) - no Life for the latter.

57.note: Scipio's siege discipline at Numantia; Marius served there as a young officer (Plutarch Marius 3) - thin coverage only.

58.periocha_anchor: in Capitolio ab optimatibus occisus est
58.note: Tribunate, deposition of Octavius, Attalus' bequest, murder of Ti. Gracchus.

59.note: Fall of Numantia, Aristonicus, death of Scipio Aemilianus, triumviral agitation.

60.periocha_anchor: C. Gracchus, Tiberii frater, tribunus plebis
60.note: C. Gracchus' legislation and colonies; Fregellae; Balearics.

61.note: Death of C. Gracchus and Fulvius Flaccus; Allobroges and Bituitus campaigns (no Life for the Gallic wars).

62.note: Micipsa's death, Jugurtha vs Adherbal; precedes Marius' involvement.

63.periocha_anchor: Cimbri, gens vaga, populabundi in Illyricum venerunt
63.note: Vestal scandal, Carbo defeated by Cimbri at Noreia.

64.note: Outbreak of Jugurthine war, Bestia's peace, 'urbem venalem'; Sallust is the main narrative witness, not Plutarch.

65.note: Metellus' Numidian campaigns with Marius as legate; Cassius killed by Tigurini.

66.periocha_anchor: vinctus ab eo et Mario traditus est
66.note: Capture of Jugurtha through Bocchus and Sulla.

67.note: Arausio, Jugurtha in Marius' triumph and execution, repeated consulships.

68.periocha_anchor: duobus deinde proeliis circa Aquas Sextias
68.note: Aquae Sextiae and Vercellae; destruction of Teutones and Cimbri.

69.note: Saturninus and Glaucia, exile of Metellus Numidicus.

70.periocha_anchor: repetundarum damnatus in exilium missus est
70.note: The 90s: Rutilius Rufus condemned, Sulla restores Ariobarzanes and meets the Parthian envoy (Plutarch Sulla 5), Drusus' beginnings.

71.note: Drusus' tribunate and murder; the Poppaedius Silo anecdote of Cato's childhood is at Cato Minor 2.

72.note: Outbreak of the Social War, massacre at Asculum; no single Life carries the Italian narrative.

73.periocha_anchor: L. Iulius Caesar consul male adversus Samnites pugnavit
73.note: Campaigns of 90 BCE; Marius against the Marsi.

74.note: Pompeius Strabo's Picene campaign; Plutarch Pompey 1 touches his father only generally.

75.periocha_anchor: L. Cornelius Sylla legatus Samnites proelio vicit
75.note: Sulla's Samnite-Hirpini successes before his consulship.

76.periocha_anchor: Asculum a Cn. Pompeio captum est
76.note: Fall of Asculum, death of Poppaedius Silo; Mithridates expels Nicomedes and Ariobarzanes.

77.periocha_anchor: L. Sylla consul cum exercitu in urbem venit
77.note: Sulpicius' laws, Sulla's march on Rome, flight of Marius (Minturnae episode). Dio frr. for 88-70 BCE are conventionally grouped as books 30-35.

78.note: Asiatic Vespers, Rhodes, Archelaus seizes Athens.

79.note: Cinna expelled, returns in arms with Marius.

80.periocha_anchor: Cinna et Marius in urbem recepti sunt
80.note: Marian massacre, seventh consulship and death of Marius.

81.periocha_anchor: L. Sylla Athenas, quas Archelaus praefectus Mithridatis occupaverat

82.periocha_anchor: copias regis, quae Macedonia occupata in Thessaliam venerant
82.note: Chaeronea and Orchomenus; Flaccus murdered by Fimbria.

83.note: Fimbria in Asia, Peace of Dardanus, death of Cinna, suicide of Fimbria.

84.periocha_anchor: novis civibus senatus consulto suffragium datum est
84.note: Failed negotiations, Carbo's faction, enfranchisement completed.

85.periocha_anchor: Sylla in Italiam cum exercitu traiecit
85.note: Landing at Brundisium, Norbanus and Scipio, young Pompey brings three legions.

86.periocha_anchor: omnem, quae in urbe erat, nobilitatem trucidavit
86.note: Young Marius consul, Damasippus' massacre, death of Scaevola; Murena's second Mithridatic war.

87.note: Sacriportus, siege of Praeneste, Rome recovered.

88.note: Colline Gate, proscriptions, death of the younger Marius.

89.note: Sullan dictatorship and legislation; Pompey in Sicily and Africa, first triumph.

90.periocha_anchor: Sylla decessit, honosque ei a senatu habitus est
90.note: Death of Sulla, Lepidus' rising, Sertorius' war opens in Spain.

91.periocha_anchor: cum imperio consulari adversus Sertorium missus est
91.note: Pompey sent to Spain with proconsular imperium.

92.periocha_anchor: Cn. Pompeius dubio eventu cum Sertorio pugnavit
92.note: Sucro and Saguntum campaigns, siege of Clunia.

93.periocha_anchor: Nicomedes Bithyniae rex populum Romanum fecit heredem
93.note: Bithynia bequeathed, Third Mithridatic War opens, Cotta beaten at Chalcedon; Sertorius' pact with Mithridates at Sertorius 23-24.

94.periocha_anchor: adversus Mithridaten equestribus proeliis feliciter pugnavit

95.periocha_anchor: Crixo et Spartaco ducibus bello excitato
95.note: Outbreak of Spartacus' revolt; relief of Cyzicus and destruction of Mithridates' army.

96.note: Murder of Sertorius by Perperna; consuls defeated by Spartacus; war given to Crassus.

97.dio: frr. books 30-35 (opening of extant book 36 lost)
97.note: End of Spartacus; Lucullus in Pontus; Pompey-Crassus consulship restores tribunician power.

98.periocha_anchor: L. Lucullus in Armenia Mithridaten et Tigranen
98.note: Tigranocerta-Armenia campaigns, mutiny, Triarius beaten at Zela; Metellus in Crete. Extant Dio begins here.

99.periocha_anchor: intra quadragesimum diem toto mari eos expulit
99.note: Lex Gabinia and the pirate war; Metellus' Cretan war and quarrel with Pompey.

100.note: Lex Manilia; Pompey takes over the Mithridatic command.

101.periocha_anchor: nocturno proelio victum coegit Bosporum profugere
101.note: Nicopolis, surrender of Tigranes, Iberian and Albanian campaigns; first Catilinarian conspiracy noticed.

102.periocha_anchor: ea coniuratio industria M. Tullii Ciceronis eruta est
102.note: Death of Mithridates, capture of Jerusalem, Catilinarian conspiracy suppressed.

103.periocha_anchor: conspiratio inter tres civitatis principes facta est
103.note: Catiline's defeat, Bona Dea, First Triumvirate, Caesar's consulship, Cicero's exile, Helvetii.

104.periocha_anchor: prima pars libri situm Germaniae moresque continet
104.note: Ariovistus, Belgae, Cicero's recall, Cato and Cyprus, Veneti.

105.periocha_anchor: Oceano in Britanniam primo parum prospere
105.note: Luca consequences, five-year provincial commands, Gabinius restores Ptolemy, Rhine crossing, Britain.

106.periocha_anchor: M. Crassus bellum Parthis inlaturus Euphraten flumen transit
106.note: Death of Julia, Ambiorix and the Sabinus disaster, Carrhae and the death of Crassus.

107.note: Great Gallic revolt (Avaricum, Gergovia); murder of Clodius, Pompey sole consul, Milo condemned.

108.periocha_anchor: C. Caesar Gallos ad Alesiam vicit
108.note: Alesia and the pacification of Gaul; succession dispute over Caesar's command.

109.periocha_anchor: causae civilium armorum et initia referuntur
109.note: Curio, crossing into Italy, Corfinium, Pompey abandons Italy.

110.periocha_anchor: C. Caesar Massiliam, quae portas cluserat, obsedit
110.note: Massilia, Ilerda, Curio destroyed by Juba in Africa, Caesar crosses to Greece.

112.note: Murder of Pompey, Alexandrian war, Cleopatra restored, Cato's desert march.

113.periocha_anchor: sine ulla belli mora victus est
113.note: African war preparations, Cato at Utica, Zela ('veni vidi vici'), Dolabella's debt agitation.

114.periocha_anchor: Caesar Scipionem praetorem Iubamque vicit ad Thapsum
114.note: Thapsus; suicides of Cato, Juba, Petreius; death of Scipio.

116.periocha_anchor: in Pompeii curia occisus est viginti tribus vulneribus
116.note: Honors, Lupercalia, the Ides of March, funeral, Octavius named heir.

117.note: Octavian arrives and takes the name; Antony's dominance, legions defect, Decimus Brutus holds Mutina.

118.periocha_anchor: M. Antonius Dec. Brutum Mutinae obsedit
118.note: Siege of Mutina begins; Octavian given propraetorian imperium; M. Brutus seizes Macedonia and C. Antonius.

119.periocha_anchor: victus deinde ab Hirtio et Caesare Antonius
119.note: Forum Gallorum and Mutina, deaths of Hirtius and Pansa, Antony joins Lepidus, Octavian consul at nineteen.

120.note: Lex Pedia, formation of the triumvirate, proscriptions, death of Cicero.

121.periocha_anchor: Dolabellam in urbe Laodicia obsessum mori coegit
121.note: Cassius masters Syria; Dolabella dies at Laodicea; C. Antonius executed.

122.note: Brutus' Thracian operations; Brutus and Cassius confer at Smyrna.

123.note: Sextus Pompeius seizes Sicily; triumvirs cross to Greece.

124.periocha_anchor: apud Philippos vario eventu adversus Brutum et Cassium
124.note: Philippi; deaths of Cassius and Brutus.

125.note: Veteran settlements, Fulvia, outbreak of the Perusine war.

126.periocha_anchor: obsessum in oppido Perusia L. Antonium

127.periocha_anchor: sororem eius Octaviam in matrimonium duxit
127.note: Labienus and the Parthians overrun Syria; pact of Brundisium and Octavia's marriage; Salvidienus; Ventidius' first victories; pact of Misenum.

128.note: War with Sextus renewed; Ventidius kills Pacorus at Gindarus; Judaea subdued (Herod installed).

129.periocha_anchor: victus deinde Pompeius in Siciliam profugit
129.note: Naulochus, Agrippa's naval crown, deposition of Lepidus.

130.note: Antony's Parthian/Median disaster and winter retreat through Armenia.

131.periocha_anchor: obpressus a legatis eius occisus est
131.note: Death of Sextus Pompeius; Octavian's Iapydes-Dalmatian-Pannonian campaigns; Artavasdes seized.

132.periocha_anchor: Caesar in Epirum cum exercitu traiecit
132.note: Breach with Antony, Donations and divorce of Octavia, declaration of war, crossing to Epirus.

133.periocha_anchor: M. Antonius ad Actium classe victus Alexandriam profugit
133.note: Actium, fall of Alexandria, deaths of Antony and Cleopatra, triple triumph; young Lepidus' plot.

134.note: Settlement of 27 BCE and the name Augustus; Gallic census; M. Crassus against Bastarnae and Moesi. No Plutarch Life covers the Augustan books.

135.note: Crassus' Thracian war, Cantabrian campaign of Augustus, conquest of the Salassi.

136.note: Periocha lost; mapped from the era block alone (approx. 24-19 BCE: completion of the Spanish wars, Parthian standards returned 20 BCE, eastern settlement).

137.note: Periocha lost; mapped from the era block alone (approx. 18-16 BCE: leges Iuliae, secular games, Lollian disaster, Augustus in Gaul).

138.periocha_anchor: Raeti a Tib. Nerone et Druso
138.note: Alpine conquest of 15 BCE; death of Agrippa; Drusus' census of Gaul.

139.periocha_anchor: civitates Germaniae cis Rhenum et trans Rhenum positae
139.note: Drusus' first German campaign; altar of the three Gauls at Lugdunum.

140.note: Piso's Thracian war, Drusus beyond the Rhine, death of Octavia.

141.note: Drusus trans-Rhenane war, Tiberius in Dalmatia-Pannonia; the periocha's notice of the Parthian standards post-dates the event of 20 BCE.

142.note: Drusus' last German campaign, his fatal fall and death, 9 BCE.
